newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine slaps ban on grain movement -trade.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine slaps ban on grain movement -trade.

text.p: Private grain buyers in Ukraine on Wednesday said the government had stopped releasing grain from state-owned elevators and farms until its orders were met -- a replay of a row that infuriated the industry a year ago.

"It's in many ways wider than it was last year," said Peter Sochan, senior policy coordinator at Citizens' Network, a U.S.-funded group set up to promote private business in Ukraine's largely state-controlled agricultural sector.
Ukrainian officials were not available for comment, but have in the past denied restricting grain movement.
But this year Serhiy Tyhypko, deputy prime minister in charge of reforms, has promised private companies they would not be barred access to grain.
Sochan said either verbal or written bans had been issued in at least half of Ukraine's 26 regions and collective farms had been ordered to pay back years of debts -- preferably in grain.
"The sense is that it's country-wide. The indication is that the initial direction is coming down from the central government," Sochan said.
Ukraine has forecast a grain harvest of 37 to 38 million tonnes this year against last year's drought-hit crop of 25.4 million tonnes.

Roger Wolfe, chairman of U.S. company Global Ag Management, said his company stood to lose $100,000 in grain it was collecting in return for debts acquired last year, when it was stopped from claiming grain in a southern region.
"There was a state order saying that until the order is fulfilled, no other persons get grain from the harvest," he said.
Sources close to the U.S. government said the embassy had called for meetings with Tyhypko to resolve the situation.
